blind_target.title: Continuous hand movement induces a far-hand bias in attentional priority.
blind_target.evidence_quote: Furthermore, on the basis of the direction effect of Festman et al. (2013a , b ), we predicted better discrimination when moving toward the probe in both tasks.
blind_target.outcome_quote: In addition, we obtained (weak) statistical evidence for a directionality effect, that is, enhanced performance when moving toward compared to away from the probe, but only in spatial gap discrimination.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Directionality was predicted in both tasks, and authors explicitly report it only in spatial discrimination. They call spatial directionality a replication of both Festman papers; aggregate across the two experiments is mixed.
